title: Served state
description: The answer `GET /api/state` serves a page's runtime, which the POST /api/event answer carries as `state` and leaf.page publishes as `/_leaf/state/*.json`: `Reading`, which `served_state.page.read_served_page` composes, with what the serving route adds. Leaf alone writes it, so nothing validates it in flight; the tests validate real readings against this schema, and the browser build generates its type from it (`build/browser/contract-types.mjs`). It is not part of the page protocol: the runtime that reads it comes from the Leaf that serves it (`runtime_selection.py`), so a change needs no bump. `leaf:event` refers to any kernel event record, `leaf:event/<kind>` to one kind's and `leaf:verb` to an x-state verb, as `registry.schema.leaf_resources` composes them; an object here adding served fields to an event record closes it again with `unevaluatedProperties`.

others.description: The machine's other live pages, each its compact row (`server_rows.py`), named by `page_key` and linked by `url` (`presence.other_leaves`). A row is open: a neighbor's Leaf may publish fields this one ignores. An export holds none.

reading.description: The news token of the facts this answer read (`served_state.reading`), which the tab's freshness reads compare.

release.description: The leaf.page release that served the page.

Reading.description: One page's state as `served_state.page.read_served_page` composes it from one transaction, before the serving route adds its neighbors and token. Before the page has an active revision, `active` and `browser` are null.

layer.description: The identity of the layer the shown revision was read under, or the page's before a revision exists (`layer-registry.md`): its generation and selection, and the fingerprint and producer of the layer the serving Leaf composes for it.

now.description: The server clock used to calibrate browser timestamps and relative ages; a laptop an hour out would otherwise date new comments an hour out too. An edge host refreshes this and `taken` together at delivery; captured event timestamps and already-folded activity keep their original dates.

working_grace_ms.description: How long working may go unheard before it reads as quiet, measured on the `now` clock. `activity` is already folded; a package dating a worker's own reports asks `quietSince`, which reads this rather than a copy.

taken.description: The moment this answer was taken, for a tab holding two. Answers cross (two sockets, one held by a proxy or a test while a later one lands, a POST's answer beside a read), and the log's sequence orders everything in a state but the reading and its data, which are hashes with no order of their own. Live answers are stamped inside their page transaction; an edge host dates a fresh read of its stored publication at delivery. The wall clock rather than a counter, which would start over with the server and make a tab open across that restart refuse every answer until the count caught up.

active.description: The revision the live root serves (`files.document_descriptor`), or null before the first.

versions.description: Each public version with its revision and address (`files.version_descriptors`).

revision.description: The immutable revision the version stamped.

revision_labels.description: Each revision's public name, `vN` or a draft's, by revision number (`files.revision_label`).

seen.description: The newest revision a tab showed the user while they were there, posted as they left (`read_state.seen_revision`), which the browser marks the page's changes since; null before any, and on a hosted copy, whose reader is not the page's user.

source_error.description: Why activating the page's authored source failed, or null.

data.description: The page's data sources as a browser reads them (`data.browser_data_from`). An answer to a tab that names this `version` in `Leaf-Data-Version` leaves out `sources`, which the tab restores from the reading it holds.

additionalProperties.description: One published source (`data.read_source`), with its publication metadata and value or validation error. Sources without a publication are omitted by `read_data`.

files.description: Each bound file's stamp, by binding, which moves when the file may have: an editor reads its file only when this stamp does.

status.description: The agent's declaration, the newest `status` event (`activity.declaration`), as `presence.presence_with_activity` reads it; that module owns the presence fields below.

state.description: `waiting` on the user or `idle`, done with the page; `waiting` before the agent declares anything.

ts.description: When the agent declared it, or when a start reopened an idle page; absent before the first declaration.

listening.description: Whether a wait lease on the page is held: the active claimant session's, or the page's own where no session claims it.

session_alive.description: Whether the claimant's lifetime stands, or null where nothing claimed the page.

live_turn.description: What the claimant's harness says of its turn now (`Harness.live_turn`), or null.

cursor.description: The acknowledgement cursor, the greatest `through` a `receipt` in the log holds: the updates through it reached their durable consumer.

pending.description: How many of the user's events past the cursor the agent hasn't taken in.

agent.description: The name the page calls its agent (`presence.page_agent`).

session_name.description: What the claimant's harness calls its session now (`Harness.session_name`), or null where it names none.

turn.description: The claimant's current turn, which an opened delivery names, or null. It and the two stamps after it are the claim's turn under the session record's names, which `state.turn_open` and `state.turn_closed` read.

turn_closed.description: When the claimant's current turn closed, or null while it is open or nothing claims the page.

turn_opened.description: When that turn opened or was last renewed, or null where nothing claims the page.

turn_takes_input.description: Whether an open turn of the claimant's takes new input before it ends (`Harness.turn_takes_input`).

input_wakes.description: Whether the nudge the claimant's next input gets would start a turn of its session's (`Harness.input_wakes`).

session_cwd.description: Where the claimant was working when it claimed the page, or null for a page nothing claimed.

activity.description: Where the agent's work on the whole page stands (`activity.py`), which the Leaf panel reads.

browser.description: The browser's reading of the shown and active revisions (`served_state.browser.browser_state`), or null before the first revision.

events.description: The log, as logged: a message's text is Markdown the page's vendored runtime renders, and its markup the fragment the CLI gate validated. The wire adds nothing, so the only vocabulary a page's frozen layer has to keep speaking is the log's own, which `$events` already stamps.

preview.description: The identity a developer preview shows in browser chrome, as `leaf-dev preview` wrote it (`server.preview_metadata`); absent on a page that is not a preview.

example.description: The name of the source file the preview serves, without its extension.

checkout.description: The checkout whose Leaf serves it.

interaction.description: `user` for a `--user` preview, whose presses reach the session that claimed it; `author` for a plain one.

input.description: The fixture publication the preview's watcher last applied.

publication.description: On leaf.page, who answers a published page and where to install Leaf; absent elsewhere.

Event.description: One logged event, exactly as `$events` declares its kind.

EventReference.description: The admitted gesture an answer or ending came from (`obligations.event_reference`).

Provenance.description: Where a Leaf payload came from (`layer.payload_provenance`): its commit and dirty bit, and its age as `committed` or `installed`.

Revision.description: One revision's live address, public stamp or draft label, and captured identity (`files.document_descriptor`).

version.description: The public version that stamped it, or null for a draft.

label.description: Its public name, `vN` or a draft's (`files.revision_label`).

executable.description: The capture's executable identity, independent of public stamps, which a client compares with its delivered document.

Subject.description: What a workflow or to-do stands on.

Activity.description: The page's one reading of agent activity (`activity.canonical_activity`), without its workflows and to-dos, which the state serves on their own.

obligations.description: The ids of the update records whose next actor is the agent: the answers it owes (`activity.canonical_activity`).

WorkKind.description: The step a harness observed the agent taking (`activity.WORK_KINDS`, read from here): working, thinking, using a tool, waiting on the user in its own window for an approval, an answer or a dialog it does not name (the `awaiting_` kinds), or replying. The browser words each one (`runtime/activity-words.js`).

ReplyEvidence.description: A provisional reply's settlement evidence, without its text (`activity._reply_evidence`).

WorkflowLine.description: A workflow's last explicit work line comes from a start record, so its text and log position arrive together (`workflows.workflow`); a failed delivery has neither.

Workflow.description: One update the user handed over that has not settled (`workflows.py`).

message.description: The message a thread input is said in, which shows its delivery: its own, or for a revision the message it rewrote.

obligation.description: The id of the obligation record this update serves (`workflows.handed_over`): its own, or for an older input in a run of turns the newest's; null for an update that owes nothing.

detail_seq.description: The log position of the start whose line `detail` is, which places the thread's working message among its messages.

anyOf.description: The failure record that answered the update.

started_by.description: The starts that take the update in hand, which the Stop hook reads.

at_work.description: Whether the agent is at work on it: at `working` or `replying`, whatever its condition.

thread.description: The thread it stands in: a thread input's own, a widget frozen into a message's thread, or null for a page widget.

Start.description: The start running on a to-do (`todos.running`).

Todo.description: One to-do, open or ended (`work_reading.WorkReading.page_todos`). The start that holds an open one is `running`; one gone quiet holds nothing.

outcome.description: How it ended: the `todo_end` in force, or the stamped version that completed it.

PlanStep.description: One step of the plan (`plans.plan_reading`): plain, or naming a to-do or obligation whose title, owner and state it shows; `done` of `total` counts its children, dropped ones left out.

Gesture.description: What an action did, in its record form's terms and its own document's words (`gesture_words.GestureWords.gesture`).

HistoryRow.description: One logged event as a history feed reads it (`history.history`). Which of the optional fields a row carries follows its kind.

Browser.description: What the browser reads of the page's revisions and the work on them (`served_state.browser.browser_state`).

basis.description: The log position the reading was taken through.

history.description: The newest rows, newest first, sent only to a page holding a widget that declares `x-history`.

views.description: Each projected revision's view, by revision number.

todos.description: Every to-do, open and ended, the one record the browser reads each from.

plan.description: The agent's outline of the work, its steps naming to-dos and obligations by id (`plans.plan_reading`), or null.

receipts.description: Every logged event a browser attempt wrote, which carries its `attempt`.

thread_memberships.description: Every thread whose history each logged event changes (`thread_context.thread_memberships`), which the browser reads for the gesture an unsent undo takes back or an unsent action replaces.

View.description: One revision's view: its document, the frozen threads as its registry reads them, and the work and undo readings drawn on it.

thread.description: The frozen threads as this revision reads them: its registry classifies their widgets' decisions, and so the obligations and attention those give.

obligations.description: Every obligation record of this view, its document's then its frozen threads', answered and withdrawn ones included. The one copy of each: a list row names an obligation by `id`.

reports.description: The view's report feed, in log order (`projection.canonical_reports`).

undo.description: The user's gestures this document can take back, newest first (`served_state.document.browser_undo_candidates`); `newest` marks the user's newest gesture, `gesture` says what that one did when it is an action, and `picked_up` marks a gesture a delivery handed into an agent's turn.

coverage.description: Each widget event and undo with the coordinate it is classified at in this view, or null.

queues.description: On me and On <agent> and what each has finished (`served_state.queues`).

spec.description: The operation the event was admitted under, by the immutable registry of the revision that interpreted it, which may differ from the active document's. Browser folds read this rather than reinterpreting history through whichever registry the current DOM selected.

absorbed.description: Whether a later revision absorbed this move, whose markup places the unit.

stands.description: Whether nothing has taken this action back or retracted it, so it stands at its coordinate once every newer one is withdrawn.

unit.description: A data record within the owning widget; its projected datum and action unit share this key.

UpdateObligationSource.description: An update the user handed over: `id` is the input's event, `subject` the thread or widget it stands on.

target.description: Where the user goes to answer: the id of a widget's prompt context, or of the thread or widget an update stands on; null for a message or page-wide task, whose source and thread supply navigation.

Obligation.description: One request and its contained answer (`obligations.py`, which owns the statuses): what a message, user task, or widget waits on the user for, or what a user update is owed (`workflows.handed_over`). The source owns the canonical value; identity includes its kind so authored ids and message ids cannot collide.

end.description: The agent's `leaf task end` that retired a question answered in words: where the answer is, or why the obligation no longer applies.

event.description: The ending's reference, which names no kind: every ending is a `todo_end`.

QueueRow.description: One row of On me or On <agent> (`served_state.queues`); `owner` names its list and `live` whether the agent has it in hand now. A record's row names its obligation by `id`, whose record is the view's `obligations` entry, and an agent to-do row names its record in the page's `todos` entry.

ObligationRow.description: An obligation record's row in On me or On <agent> (`served_state.queues`).

id.description: The obligation, whose record is the view's `obligations` entry.

owner.description: The list the row stands on.

thread.description: The thread it stands in, or null.

also.description: The other obligations the user answers at the same place, each a view's `obligations` entry: the further records a thread's reply answers, and on an obligation's row those of a thread about it.

live.description: Whether the agent has it in hand now: an update it is at work on whose work has not gone quiet or stopped.

TodoRow.description: An agent to-do's row in On <agent> (`served_state.queues`).

id.description: The to-do, whose record is the page's `todos` entry.

owner.description: The list the row stands on.

thread.description: The thread it stands in, or null.

live.description: Whether a start holds the to-do now.

DoneRow.description: A row that left its list, in the Done of the list `owner` names: how it ended (`state`), when (`ended`, null going last), and the outcome's detail.

Anchor.description: Where a thread stands on the page, as a comment, reply or reanchor names it, or null.

Message.description: A message as a served thread holds it.

anyOf.description: A logged comment or reply, with its current content version (`read_state.content_version`), which the browser marks read once its words have been shown. An agent's message carries the name it is shown under as `agent` (`schema.agent_name`). An input's first answer carries `key`, the name a provisional reply and the answer that retires it share.

completed_by.description: The ordinary or provisional reply that supersedes this progress message. Hide it only while that reply is presented.

edited.description: The user's latest rewrite, and the words it replaced.

anyOf.description: A provisional reply streaming under a delivery attempt, which joins its thread once it has words (`served_state.thread.browser_thread`).

ContentVersion.description: One version of an agent message's content: the message, and its latest edit's id or else its own (`read_state.content_version`).

version.description: The content version's id, which a `read` event names.

Attention.description: Whose turn a thread is (`served_state.browser._thread_attention`), read from the open obligation records in it: a widget's or an update's handed back on the user, else one on the agent, whose strongest serving workflow it names; or null for nobody's.

todo.description: The id of the to-do the thread waits on, whose record is the page's `todos` entry.

Thread.description: One thread, keyed by the comment that opened it (`events.build_threads`), as `served_state.thread.browser_thread` serves it.

revisions.description: The user's edits in log order, each with `was`, the words it replaced.

resolved.description: What closed the thread, an agent's named by `agent` (`schema.agent_name`), or null while it is open.

seat.description: The widget whose thread seat the root stands in (`events.seat_root`), or null.

summaries.description: The thread's current summaries (`events.active_summaries`); `protected` lists the covered messages a summary must not hide.

unread.description: The content versions the user hasn't read (`read_state.unread_content`).

Stage.description: How far an update has reached the agent; `answered` is only ever a retained failed response.

ViewAnswer.description: The answer `GET /api/view` gives (`served_state.service.PageStateService.page_browser_view`): one revision's browser reading at an exact log boundary, which version comparison folds.

EventAnswer.description: The answer `POST /api/event` gives once its gates pass (`event_endpoint`).

anyOf.description: Accepted, with the page's state, which holds the event's receipt.

Refused, and final: nothing was appended. `error` is the words the tab shows its user. A refusal admission made carries `state`, which restores the tab from current truth; a gate's refusal (`http.PageEndpoint._refuse`) carries none.

attempt.description: The posted `attempt`, echoed as it came.

anyOf.description: A fault that may have landed either side of the append, so the next identical request finds out (`event_endpoint.event_fault`).

attempt.description: The posted `attempt`, echoed as it came.

Finding.description: What a refusal refused on (`findings.Finding.json`, less its words). The browser shows the refusal's `error` instead.

SampleAnswer.description: The answer `POST /api/samples` gives: the new live sample's address, and its interaction page (`http.PageEndpoint._create_sample`).

MediaAnswer.description: The answer `POST /api/media` gives: the stored image's page-relative path (`media.store_uploaded_media`).

FileSnapshot.description: One bound file as `GET` and a successful `POST /api/files/<binding>` answer it (`file_bindings`): its name, its text with LF line endings, and the revision a save names.

StaleFile.description: A save refused because the file changed since the revision it named, with the file as it is now.

Refusal.description: Any route's refusal of a request (`http.PageEndpoint._refuse`): the words the page shows.

LayerAnswer.description: A write held because the tab speaks another layer (`http.PageEndpoint._layer_gate`): the generation it should speak, which the `Leaf-Layer` header also carries, so the tab reloads without reading this.
